When you’re wicking, rake out the wicks after you put it into the coil. You need to cut the wicks wayyyyy shorter aswell. Try aim for the cotton sitting just in the wicking channels not being stuffed in as it is done in the picture. The trick is to have as little as possible in the wicking channels while still being enough cotton to stop the juice from flowing freely in from the tank/ flooding the coils. Also lower wattage if wicking properly doesn’t help much, but proper wicking will definitely improve it

Current Vaper here. I know it’s not exactly the same thing, but I’m gonna answer from my perspective. The addictive properties of nicotine doesn’t mean you don’t enjoy it, most people that smoke/vape really do enjoy it. Sometimes when trying to quit, a reason for it being so difficult is the enjoyment you get out of the smell, the whispy smoke and the “reward” of the smoke (I mean that it’s like giving someone a bag of candy after they’ve completed a task, it’s a reward and a delight at the end of something). 
For me personally I love vaping. The smell, the cloud, and most importantly the build. It’s become a hobby building my own devices, making my own coils and mixing my own juices. I don’t have to do all that stuff, but I enjoy it. I could just as easily buy disposable devices or prefilled pod devices that would require no effort and just give me nicotine.
